lesson.title: Carving Out a Gap: How Band-Reject Filters Work
lesson.summary: A band-reject filter is the mirror image of a band-pass filter: it attenuates a band of frequencies between a lower and upper cutoff while passing everything below and above that band.
lesson.body:
Where a band-pass filter, from Band-Pass Filter, lets a range of frequencies through and blocks everything else, a band-reject filter, sometimes called a band-stop filter, does the exact opposite: it blocks a range of frequencies between a lower cutoff fL and an upper cutoff fH, and passes everything outside that band. The general filter language from Filter still applies, only now the stopband sits in the middle of the frequency axis instead of at one end.

One way to build a band-reject filter is to place a parallel LC tank, the circuit from Parallel Resonance, directly in the signal path in series with the load. Away from the tank's resonant frequency its impedance is low, so it passes the signal through with little loss. Right at resonance, the tank's impedance rises to its peak, choking off that frequency while barely disturbing anything else. A second common approach places a series LC branch as a shunt to ground instead: at resonance the series branch's impedance collapses toward zero, briefly shorting that frequency to ground while leaving other frequencies mostly alone.

Just as with the band-pass filter, the width of the rejected region is its bandwidth, the same quantity from Bandwidth, measured as BW = fH minus fL.

Suppose a band-reject filter needs to reject frequencies from fL = 950 Hz to fH = 1050 Hz. The bandwidth is BW = 1050 minus 950, which is 100 Hz. The center of the rejected band sits at roughly f0 approximately 1000 Hz, for a narrow band like this the arithmetic mean of fL and fH is a good approximation to the true geometric-mean center. The quality factor is Q = f0/BW = 1000/100 = 10, a fairly narrow, selective rejection in the frequency response. As that rejected band gets narrower and narrower relative to its center frequency, the circuit becomes what is specifically called a notch filter, covered next.
